questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of India, and how long did he serve?
questions.a: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister, serving from 1947 to 1964. A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing the timeline of Independence with later leaders.

questions.q: What does it mean for a country to be "secular," based on Nehru’s policies?
questions.a: It means the state does not favor any specific religion and treats all citizens equally regardless of their faith. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks secularism means "no religion at all" or "banning religion," which is incorrect.

questions.q: If a village has both a government-run post office and privately owned shops, which economic system is it following?
questions.a: It is following a mixed economy. The steps are: (1) Identify that government control exists (post office), (2) identify that private ownership exists (shops), (3) conclude that both co-existing means a mixed economy. A wrong answer reveals confusion between pure socialism and mixed systems.

questions.q: Why was it important for Nehru to establish the Election Commission right after independence?
questions.a: It was important to ensure that the transfer of power and future leadership were decided by the people, not by force. A wrong answer implies the student doesn't understand the link between democracy and regular elections.

questions.q: Could India have functioned as a democracy if the government had chosen to favor one religion over all others? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, because democracy relies on equality; favoring one religion would make other citizens feel like "second-class" members, likely causing conflict and breaking the unity of the nation. A wrong answer shows a lack of understanding of the connection between secularism and social stability.

questions.q: If you were starting a new country today, which of Nehru’s three pillars—democracy, secularism, or a mixed economy—would you prioritize first, and why?
questions.a: A good answer will choose one and explain it through the lens of stability (e.g., "I would choose democracy because it gives everyone a voice"). A poor answer provides a preference without explaining how it keeps the country united.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Nehru Era refers to the period from 1947 to 1964 when Jawaharlal Nehru served as India’s first Prime Minister, ______ the foundations of the nation's democratic, secular, and economic framework.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are asked to build a new house for a large family that has just moved in; how would you decide on the rules for ______ to live together peacefully?

Fill in the blank: Nehru faced a similar task in ______—he had to organize a vast, diverse country into a single, functioning "home." Start by thinking of the Parliament and the Election Commission as the "rules" of the house that keep it orderly.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to list three key pillars of Nehru’s nation-building (democracy, secularism, and mixed economy) and explain why each was important for a newly independent country.
